- Progressive right knee swelling and pain with prior left knee involvement → supports asymmetric, sequential, inflammatory oligoarthritis.  
- No fever, erythema, or warmth → argues against acute septic arthritis or florid gout flare, favoring subacute/chronic inflammatory process.  
- Negative RF and anti-CCP → excludes seropositive rheumatoid arthritis.  
- Elevated ESR and CRP → confirms active systemic inflammation, inconsistent with non-inflammatory causes.  
- 16-year history of undiagnosed “arthritis” → suggests chronic, possibly under-recognized inflammatory arthropathy.  
- No recent infection, injury, or dental procedures → lowers likelihood of reactive arthritis or post-traumatic synovitis.  

[GAPS]  
- Absence of assessment for psoriatic skin/nail changes (e.g., pitting, onycholysis, scalp plaques).  
- No evaluation for dactylitis, enthesitis (e.g., Achilles, plantar fascia), or spinal symptoms (e.g., morning stiffness >30 min, nocturnal back pain).  
- Pending synovial fluid analysis — critical to exclude crystal-induced or low-grade infectious synovitis.  
- Pending HLA-B27 — would support spondyloarthropathy but is not required for diagnosis.  
- No imaging (US/MRI) to assess for bone marrow edema, enthesophytes, or erosions characteristic of PsA or SpA.  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Psoriatic arthritis
